title: relay queue becomes a package with its handler
what: Move `relay queue` out of bin/relay as one package, verbatim: lib/relay_cmd/queue/__init__.py holds `QUEUE_USAGE` (as `USAGE`), `_queue_options`, `QUEUE_WRITES` and the handler `cmd_queue` (as `run(args)`), still one function with its if-chain of actions; splitting it into one module per action is move 8, not this one. The package header has `USAGE`, `WRITES = False` for its bare use. Delete them from bin/relay (`QUEUE_USAGE` through `cmd_queue`) and from COMMANDS and the docstring.
- If bin/relay carries a module-size marker line (from the module-size test, move 2), this move drops it: bin/relay leaves the over-limit set in this move.

- The guard is not edited. Its table still answers every queue word, and the package's bare `WRITES = False` is never consulted for add/take/start/... (guard resolution order: action module, then the guard's table, then the module). Check by running the guard's frozen verdicts after the move.

- Move 3 as built: tests/relay_commands.py `queue_words()` already follows the usage into lib/relay_cmd/queue/__init__.py (USAGE_FILES) and tests/test_cmd_files.py walks the package; the tests then need tests/test_cmd_queue.py for the package's own use. Convention: `relay queue --help` prints the usage lines printed before the move (literal); the smoke case `relay queue count` in a temporary git repository (via run_relay(git=True)) asserts exit 0 and the "count" line. The existing tests/test_cmd_smoke.py case for queue (exit 2, "relay queue: not a git repository") must stay green.
- Tests that import queue functions from bin/relay (grep `load_relay\|bin/relay` in tests/) must load them from the package.
Done: full gate green; `relay queue` behaves exactly as before; bin/relay is smaller by about 250 lines.

Module interface (every moved command): `USAGE: str` whose first line is `relay <cmd> ...`; `WRITES: bool`; optional `READ_FLAGS` (sync's `--dry`); `def run(args: list[str]) -> int`. Names match [a-z][a-z0-9_]*, a typed `-` maps to `_`. A package's `__init__.py` has the header `USAGE`, `WRITES` for its bare use, and an optional `fallback(args)`; mixed commands (queue, check, improve, bench, license) become packages with one module per action.

Test convention (tests/cmd_harness.py docstring, move 3): each command's own test file tests/test_cmd_<cmd>.py (tests/test_cmd_<cmd>_<action>.py for an action of a package) holds two cases: (1) `relay <cmd> --help` prints the usage lines it printed before the move, copied as a literal; (2) one smoke case with harmless arguments asserting the exit code and one output line, run through `run_relay` from tests/cmd_harness.py (it returns code, stdout, stderr and the files written, in temporary HOME, RELAY_HOME, RELAY_ROOT and cwd). For a command that cannot run in a temporary tree, the case is its usage refusal. tests/test_cmd_files.py fails, naming the file, for any module under lib/relay_cmd/ without its test file. tests/test_cmd_smoke.py already holds one table SMOKE with a case per command (all 21); keep the moved command's case there working, and note that under the empty RELAY_ROOT calibrate, install, flows, rules and doctor fail on a missing file before they read their arguments, so for those the command's own file must replace the case with one whose outcome depends on an argument. This catches an off-by-one in how the dispatcher hands args to run() (with or without the command name), which the help tests (they stop before run) and ruff do not see.

After the move, in the same change: delete the moved commands from bin/relay's docstring, COMMANDS and imports (same commit as the new modules; commit A is "moved verbatim", reviewed with `git diff -M --color-moved=zebra`); do not edit plugins/delegate/hooks/read-only-guard.py (the guard keeps its table until move 10); rewrite the `where` of open queue items that name the moved commands in bin/relay to the new module files, and record how many items the start filter holds before and after. tests/relay_commands.py (names(), queue_words()) already reads the module walk joined with bin/relay's COMMANDS, so the help test and the guard completeness test need no edit.

Start rule: the move takes named top-level functions and constants out of bin/relay. It starts when no running lane has changed anything it takes: read a lane's change with `git diff -U0 master...<lane> -- bin/relay` and compare each hunk's line range on master with the spans of the taken names (a hunk inside another function does not block). The item names bin/relay, so the start filter refuses it; start it with `relay queue start --despite-wait` when this rule says it is free. If a lane holding a taken function has not landed within 60 minutes, start anyway and that lane ports its hunk. Before landing, read again: the move lands whatever the second read shows; a lane that changed a moved function ports its hunk when it takes the default branch (git shows a conflict in the deleted function; the fixer reapplies the hunk to the new module); the landing note names the lane, the function and the new file.

Traps for this move: keep imports lint-clean (ruff F; a dropped import of a helper is ruff F821); tests that import from the repo root must still run under the short gate; done items name their `test` ids, which are found by name, so do not rename tests; RULE_TESTS names in lib/relay_textonly.py must stay valid; tests never touch the live .relay/queue (use a temporary folder); a move that takes a function another running lane changed ports that lane's hunk by hand (start rule below); the size marker leaves a file in the move that brings it under 600 lines.
why: Move 7 of the split of relay into one module per subcommand. The owner decided it on 28 Oct: "каждая подкоманда может и должна жить в своем модуле, этот подход должен быть распространен на весь relay". Waits for move 6 (setup, migrate, install, doctor, sync) and the done fix that made `start` a writing queue word. The shared-file pairs among open items fall to 10; bin/relay also drops below the size limit, so its size marker goes.
